# Research Report: Encoding Professional Methodology into Agent Artifacts — What Exists (2025–2026)

Scope: what the NanoClaw-based startup can adopt or learn from, across (1) Anthropic Agent Skills, (2) workflow/playbook encoding in agent products, (3) "teach the agent your process" mechanisms, (4) role-based template libraries, (5) adoption evidence — then answers to the three key questions.

---

## 1. Anthropic Agent Skills — the SKILL.md substrate

### 1.1 Exact format (open spec)

Anthropic published Agent Skills as an **open standard** (spec at [agentskills.io/specification](https://agentskills.io/specification), reference repo [github.com/agentskills/agentskills](https://github.com/agentskills/agentskills)). Per third-party reporting, the open standard was released Dec 18, 2025 and has been adopted by 26+ platforms including OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code ([agensi.io overview](https://www.agensi.io/learn/agent-skills-open-standard) — adoption count is that source's claim, I could not independently verify "26+").

A skill is a directory whose only required file is `SKILL.md`:

```
skill-name/
├── SKILL.md          # required: YAML frontmatter + markdown instructions
├── scripts/          # optional executable code (run, not loaded into context)
├── references/       # optional docs loaded on demand
└── assets/           # optional templates/data
```

Frontmatter fields (from the [spec](https://agentskills.io/specification)):
- `name` (required, ≤64 chars, lowercase/digits/hyphens, must match directory name)
- `description` (required, ≤1024 chars — must say *what it does AND when to use it*, with trigger keywords)
- optional: `license`, `compatibility` (≤500 chars, env requirements), `metadata` (arbitrary k/v, e.g. author/version), `allowed-tools` (experimental, pre-approved tools)

**Progressive disclosure** is the core design ([Anthropic engineering post](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)):
1. **Level 1 — metadata** (~100 tokens/skill): all skills' name+description injected into system prompt at startup.
2. **Level 2 — SKILL.md body** (<5,000 tokens / <500 lines recommended): read via filesystem tool only when the model judges the skill relevant.
3. **Level 3+ — bundled files**: references/scripts loaded or executed on demand; "the amount of context that can be bundled into a skill is effectively unbounded" because scripts execute without entering context.

### 1.2 What makes a GOOD skill (Anthropic's own guidance)

From the [engineering blog](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills) and the [skill authoring best-practices doc](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices) — the best-practices page is the single most relevant document for your "methodology pack" idea:

- **Conciseness**: "Claude is already very smart" — only add context the model lacks; every loaded token competes with conversation history.
- **Degrees of freedom matched to task fragility**: high freedom (heuristic text) for judgment tasks like code review; medium (parameterized pseudocode); low freedom ("run exactly this script, do not modify") for fragile sequences. This maps directly onto professional methodology: judgment steps vs. deterministic steps.
- **Workflow + checklist pattern**: for complex multi-step processes, embed a copyable checklist the agent checks off as it progresses (their canonical multi-step workflow pattern — exactly the "core moment chain" shape).
- **Feedback loops**: run validator → fix → repeat; "plan-validate-execute" with machine-verifiable intermediate artifacts (e.g. a `changes.json` validated by script before execution).
- **Template pattern & examples pattern**: bundle output templates (strict or flexible) and input→output example pairs.
- **Conditional workflow pattern**: decision points routing to sub-workflows, pushed into separate files if large.
- **Description is the trigger**: written in third person, with explicit "Use when…" phrasing and keywords; Claude picks from potentially 100+ skills by description alone.
- **Evaluation-driven development**: build 3+ evals *before* writing the skill; baseline without the skill; iterate. There is no built-in eval runner — you roll your own.
- **Iterate with Claude itself**: "Claude A" authors/refines the skill, "Claude B" (fresh instance) tests it; capture successful approaches and mistakes back into the skill.
- Anti-patterns: vague names (`helper`, `utils`), too many alternative approaches, nested reference chains >1 level deep, time-sensitive info, magic constants in scripts.

### 1.3 Discovery/loading in Claude Code and the Agent SDK

- **Agent SDK** ([docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/skills)): skills load from `.claude/skills/` (project) and `~/.claude/skills/` (user) only if `settingSources`/`setting_sources` includes those sources (SDK loads no filesystem settings by default), and `"Skill"` must be in `allowed_tools`. Plugin-bundled skills are namespaced `plugin-name:skill-name` ([plugins in the SDK](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/plugins)). Directly relevant to NanoClaw since it runs on the Agent SDK.
- **Claude Code** ([skills doc](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)) extends the open standard with features that matter a lot for methodology packs:
  - **Invocation control**: `disable-model-invocation: true` (only user can trigger, e.g. `/deploy` — for side-effectful workflows where the human controls timing) and `user-invocable: false` (background knowledge only the model loads). Default: both can invoke.
  - `when_to_use` field — extra trigger phrases appended to description (combined cap 1,536 chars in the listing).
  - **Arguments**: `$ARGUMENTS`, `$0/$1`, named `arguments:` — a skill is parameterizable like a command ("one sentence → whole chain runs" is literally `/end-of-call <client>`).
  - **Subagent execution**: `context: fork` + `agent:` runs the skill in a forked subagent context.
  - `allowed-tools` (pre-approved permissions while active), `disallowed-tools`, `model`, `effort`, per-skill `hooks`, `paths` (activate only for matching files), dynamic context injection via `` !`command` `` blocks.
  - **State/lifecycle limits**: invoked skill content enters the conversation once and is *not re-read*; on auto-compaction only the first 5,000 tokens of each recent skill are re-attached under a combined 25,000-token budget — older skills can drop out entirely. There is **no built-in persistent state machine**: state across a multi-step workflow must live in the conversation, in files the skill writes, or in checklists.
  - Custom slash commands have been merged into skills (a `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and a skill are now the same mechanism).

### 1.4 Marketplace situation

- **Official**: [anthropics/skills GitHub repo](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) (doubles as a Claude Code plugin marketplace via `marketplace.json`; install e.g. `/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills`); a curated [anthropics/claude-plugins-official](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-plugins-official) directory; and in the Claude apps a **unified in-product directory** (Customize > Skills > Browse skills) featuring partner-built skills from Notion, Figma, Atlassian etc. ([help center](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14328846-browse-skills-connectors-and-plugins-in-one-directory), [skills announcement](https://claude.com/blog/skills)). I found no evidence that a standalone `skills.claude.com` site exists — the directory lives inside the product; treat "skills.claude.com" as unconfirmed. **No official paid marketplace exists**; Anthropic has only signaled interest in community contributions ([claudeskills.info](https://claudeskills.info/skills/) reporting).
- **Third-party**: [awesome-claude-skills](https://github.com/travisvn/awesome-claude-skills), [claudeskills.info](https://claudeskills.info/skills/) (~140+ free skills), [skillsdirectory.com](https://www.skillsdirectory.com/), various personal marketplaces on GitHub. All small/curated.
- **Cautionary tale — ClawHub (OpenClaw's skill marketplace)**: grew from ~2,857 to 10,700+ skills in weeks, and security audits found **341 malicious skills** (Koi Security, later 824+ as the marketplace grew), typosquatting, scanner-evasion (payloads hidden in oversized READMEs), and ranking manipulation ([The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/02/researchers-find-341-malicious-clawhub.html), [Unit 42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/openclaw-ai-supply-chain-risk/), [Dark Reading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyber-risk/malicious-openclaw-skills-clawhub-threaten-ai-supply-chain), [Silverfort](https://www.silverfort.com/blog/clawhub-vulnerability-enables-attackers-to-manipulate-rankings-to-become-the-number-one-skill/)). Lesson: skills are prompt-injection + supply-chain surface; a curated, signed, first-party pack library beats an open marketplace for a trust-sensitive product.
- **Expert assessment**: Simon Willison, ["Claude Skills are awesome, maybe a bigger deal than MCP"](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Oct/16/claude-skills/) (Oct 16, 2025): skills are "markdown with a tiny bit of YAML," trivially shareable, and outsource the hard parts to the harness — vs. MCP's protocol weight and token cost.

---

## 2. How workflow/agent products package "a multi-step professional workflow"

| Product | Unit of packaging | Trigger model | Template library |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lindy.ai** | A "Lindy" = agent with trigger + steps (flow-chart style), built in natural language; Lindies can call each other ("societies of agents") | Event triggers (new email, call ended, form, schedule); multi-trigger workflows, loops, conditions | 50+ pre-built templates organized by use case (sales, support, meetings, email) and industry ([templates docs](https://docs.lindy.ai/fundamentals/lindy-101/templates), [template categories](https://www.lindy.ai/template-categories/workflow-automation)) |
| **Dust.tt** | An agent = plain-English **instructions** + tools + company data sources; new **"Skills"** feature packages instructions+knowledge+tools into reusable modules shared across all workspace agents — update once, all agents benefit ([changelog](https://docs.dust.tt/changelog/skills-share-expertise-across-all-your-agents)) | @-mention in Slack/chat, native triggers (schedule/webhook), or external orchestrators (Zapier/Make/n8n) ([blog](https://dust.tt/blog/automate-dust-agents-workflow-tools)) | Team-oriented agent examples rather than a big public template store; semantic layer over company knowledge is the differentiator ([product](https://dust.tt/home/product)) |
| **Relevance AI** | **"Workforce"** = a team of agents that "automate entire playbooks — triggered by events or signals," each agent owning a step and handing off context ([workforce page](https://relevanceai.com/workforce)); flagship Bosh (BDR) is a multi-agent system with delegating sub-agents ([Bosh docs](https://relevanceai.com/docs/agent/agent-examples/bosh-bdr-agent)) | Event/signal triggers or chat | Public [agent marketplace/templates](https://relevanceai.com/templates) organized **by role** (SDR, AE, RevOps, recruiter…) and by task |
| **Zapier Agents** (successor to Zapier Central) | **"Behavior"** = trigger + natural-language instructions + connected apps; an agent bundles several behaviors + data sources | Any of Zapier's 7,000+ app triggers, chat, buttons, or invocation from a Zap ([build an agent](https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/24393442652557-Build-an-agent-in-Zapier-Agents), [trigger setup](https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/45394909914381-Set-up-your-agent-s-trigger)) | Growing template library with preset instructions+apps per business function (Lead Qualification & Scoring, Call Follow-Up Assistant, Candidate Ranking…) — editable after instantiation ([agents guide](https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents-guide/)) |
| **Relay.app** | **"Playbook"** = trigger + step sequence with human-in-the-loop steps; an "Agent" is an AI teammate that *owns a set of workflows* (role = bundle of playbooks — closest existing model to your "role pack") ([docs](https://docs.relay.app/agents/agents), [how it works](https://www.relay.app/how-it-works)) | App triggers, schedules, manual; "mini AI agents" as steps inside deterministic flows ([blog](https://www.relay.app/blog/how-to-add-a-mini-ai-agent-to-your-workflow)) | Playbooks are explicitly "repeatable, teachable processes" — templated, shared, refined |
| **Gumloop** | Flow (node graph); agents pick tools mid-task via MCP | Triggers via cloud platform, browser extension | Deep template library by domain: HR/hiring, sales/CRM, legal, SEO, docs ([comparison](https://www.gumloop.com/vs/n8n)) |
| **n8n** | Workflow JSON with an AI Agent node + sub-nodes (model, memory, tools) | Any node trigger; chat requires a separate Chat Trigger node | ~10,400 community templates, ~7,100 in the AI category ([n8n workflows](https://n8n.io/workflows/), [AI category](https://n8n.io/workflows/categories/ai/)) |

**Takeaway for the startup:** the market's dominant unit is *trigger + instructions + connected tools* ("behavior"/"playbook"), with role-level packaging appearing only as (a) Relay's "agent owns a set of workflows," (b) Relevance's multi-agent "workforce playbooks," and (c) Dust's cross-agent "Skills" modules. Nobody yet ships a portable, open-format *role methodology pack*; everyone's packaging is platform-locked. Anthropic's SKILL.md is the only open, portable substrate in the list.

---

## 3. "Teach the agent your process" mechanisms

- **Demonstration capture (SOP tools)**: [Scribe](https://scribe.com/library/scribe-vs-tango) and [Tango](https://www.tango.ai/) record a user performing a workflow in the browser and auto-generate step-by-step guides with screenshots; Tango now ships "Tango Agents" on top of captured SOPs (product details thin — uncertain how agentic it really is). These produce *human-readable* SOPs, which are exactly the raw material a SKILL.md compiler could ingest.
- **Demonstration → automation**: [Optexity](https://optexity.com/blog/the-best-production-ready-browser-automation-platforms-in-2026) generates deterministic browser automations from a screen recording ("demonstrate once, deploy via API"). The broader 2026 agentic-browser landscape treats "teach mode" (show once, agent repeats) as an established pattern ([landscape guide](https://nohacks.co/blog/agentic-browser-landscape-2026)). I did not find a mature *chat-agent* product that learns a professional's methodology purely from watching — this appears to be genuinely open ground.
- **Interview-based teaching (Anthropic patterns)** — most directly adoptable for NanoClaw:
  - **`/init`** bootstraps CLAUDE.md by having the agent explore the environment; an enhanced interactive multi-phase init flow exists (`CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1`) ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)).
  - **AskUserQuestion interview pattern**: Anthropic's own recommended practice is "have Claude interview you first" using the AskUserQuestion tool before big work — the exact mechanism for calibrating a generic role pack to an individual ([best practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)).
  - **Memory layering**: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (personal), `./CLAUDE.md` (shared), `CLAUDE.local.md` (private), plus auto-memory (MEMORY.md) written back autonomously ([memory guide](https://joseparreogarcia.substack.com/p/claude-code-memory-explained), [memory tool docs](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)). Community consensus: keep CLAUDE.md ~80–120 high-signal lines; procedures belong in skills, facts in CLAUDE.md ([Claude Code skills doc](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills): "create a skill… when a section of CLAUDE.md has grown into a procedure rather than a fact").
  - **Skill self-authoring**: Anthropic explicitly recommends "ask Claude to capture its successful approaches and common mistakes into reusable context and code within a skill," and states plans for agents to create/edit/evaluate skills autonomously ([engineering post](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)). So the "teach by doing it once together, then crystallize into a skill" loop (Claude A authors / Claude B tests) is Anthropic's own documented workflow — adopt it verbatim.
- **Zapier Central** (predecessor of Agents) let users teach "behaviors" conversationally and correct the agent's drafts over time ([community post](https://community.zapier.com/p/zapier-central)); Zapier Agents kept the natural-language instructions + editable behaviors model.

---

## 4. Role-based agent template libraries

- **Relevance AI** — most explicit "role as product": named AI teammates (Bosh the BDR/SDR, Apla account research, Lima lifecycle marketing) plus a [template marketplace](https://relevanceai.com/templates) organized by role pages (e.g. [SDR agent templates](https://relevanceai.com/agent-templates-roles/sales-development-representative-sdr-ai-agents-1), recruiter templates). Templates instantiate into your workspace and are calibrated by connecting CRM/data sources and editing instructions.
- **Beam.ai** — [library of production-ready agent templates](https://beam.ai/agents), each shipping with configured workflows, integration setups, and setup guidance; 1,500+ integrations ([template blog](https://beam.ai/agentic-insights/5-ready-to-use-ai-agent-templates-that-save-40-hours-per-week)).
- **Lindy.ai** — 50+ role/use-case templates instantiated as editable Lindies ([docs](https://docs.lindy.ai/fundamentals/lindy-101/templates)).
- **CrewAI** — role-based by construction (`role`, `goal`, `backstory` per agent, YAML-config recommended) ([agents docs](https://docs.crewai.com/en/concepts/agents)); recruiting crews (sourcing → screening → matching → evaluation agents) are a canonical community project ([ProjectPro](https://www.projectpro.io/article/crew-ai-projects-ideas-and-examples/1117)) — but it's a dev framework, not an end-user template product.
- **MindStudio** — no-code visual builder with templates and NL-to-workflow generation ([vs CrewAI](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/mindstudio-vs-crewai)). **Voiceflow**: conversational-agent templates, mostly support/voice — I did not verify role-pack depth there (uncertain).
- **Calibration mechanisms observed across all of these** (thin everywhere): (1) connect your data sources/apps (the template's variables), (2) edit the natural-language instructions after instantiation, (3) upload brand/knowledge docs, (4) chat-based refinement of drafts. Nobody I found does a structured *methodology interview* ("walk me through what you do after a sales call, what does 'qualified' mean for you, who gets the brief") that compiles answers into the template's parameters. Jotform/Pipefy market "clarifying questions" onboarding for narrow customer-onboarding agents ([Pipefy](https://www.pipefy.com/blog/customize-customer-onboarding-ai-agents/)), but that's for end-customer flows, not professional calibration.

---

## 5. Adoption evidence (what gets traction)

Hard public numbers are scarce; here's what exists:

- **n8n**: ~10,400 community templates; ~7,100 in the AI category; per one tracker, **AI-agent templates ≈78% of new submissions** (30-day window, May 2026) and multi-agent templates doubled in two months to ~¼ of the AI category ([n8n workflows](https://n8n.io/workflows/), [connectsafely analysis](https://connectsafely.ai/articles/n8n-templates-workflow-automation-examples) — third-party analysis, treat percentages as approximate).
- **Relevance AI**: $37M+ raised (Series B $24M, May 2025); **40,000 agents built in a single January**; customers incl. Canva, Databricks, KPMG, Activision ([SaaStr](https://www.saastr.com/saastr-ai-app-of-the-week-relevance-ai-the-platform-where-ops-teams-build-entire-ai-workforces-without-writing-a-line-of-code/)). Its flagship, most-marketed template is a *sales* role (Bosh BDR) — consistent with sales/SDR being the wedge.
- **ClawHub**: ~2,800 → 10,700+ skills within weeks of launch — demonstrates huge appetite for installable agent skills, and equally the security downside ([eSecurity Planet](https://www.esecurityplanet.com/threats/hundreds-of-malicious-skills-found-in-openclaws-clawhub/)).
- **Zapier's public template lists** skew to sales/revops (lead qualification, call follow-up) and recruiting (candidate ranking) ([guide](https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-agents-guide/)).
- **Which roles win**: no rigorous public breakdown found. Directional evidence (what vendors lead with, template category sizes) points to **sales/SDR first, support second, recruiting third** — but I'm marking this as inference, not measured fact.
- Gartner (via [IBM](https://www.ibm.com/think/ai-agents) roundup): 40% of enterprise apps to embed task-specific agents by end-2026, up from <5% in 2025 — context, not product-level evidence.
- No public adoption numbers exist yet for Anthropic's skills directory or the anthropics/skills repo beyond GitHub activity (uncertain).

---

## Answers to the key questions

**(a) Is SKILL.md the right substrate for "role methodology packs"? What are its limits?**

Yes, with a composition layer on top. Strengths: open standard, portable across 20+ harnesses, progressive disclosure keeps a fat methodology pack token-cheap, `scripts/` gives deterministic steps (CRM writes, formatting), `assets/` gives output templates, Claude Code/SDK extensions give you arguments (`/end-of-call acme`), invocation control, per-skill tool permissions, and subagent forking. Anthropic's checklist/feedback-loop/conditional-workflow patterns in the [best-practices doc](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices) are literally "professional methodology encoding" patterns.

Limits to engineer around:
1. **Triggering is probabilistic** — it hinges entirely on the 1,024-char description (1,536 incl. `when_to_use` in Claude Code). For "core moments" you should not rely on ambient triggering: use explicit invocation (one sentence → `/skill` with args), or NanoClaw-level event routing (message classifier → skill), and `disable-model-invocation` for side-effectful chains.
2. **No native chaining/orchestration** — skills don't declare dependencies or call each other; composition happens implicitly via the model. A "role pack" therefore needs a top-level router skill (or CLAUDE.md section) mapping core moments → member skills, or plugin packaging to bundle them.
3. **No state** — skill content is injected once, not re-read; compaction can truncate to 5k tokens per skill / 25k total. Multi-turn workflow state must live in workspace files (NanoClaw already has this pattern with CLAUDE.local.md) or checklists the agent writes.
4. **No built-in eval/QA or paid distribution**; open marketplaces are a proven malware vector (ClawHub) — curate and sign your packs.

**(b) State of the art in packaging a ROLE (not a task) as an installable artifact?**

Immature — this is the gap. Closest existing models: Relay.app's *agent = owner of a set of playbooks*; Relevance AI's *workforce = playbook as a coordinated agent team* plus role-organized template marketplace; Dust's *Skills = shared expertise modules across agents*; Claude Code *plugins* (bundle of namespaced skills + commands + hooks + MCP config) — technically the best "role pack" container in the Anthropic ecosystem, since one install delivers a coherent set of skills. Nobody ships a portable "AI Chief-of-Staff methodology, v1.2" that installs across platforms; everything is walled-garden. A role pack = plugin{router + N core-moment skills + calibration file + scripts} on the Agent SDK would be genuinely novel packaging on an open substrate.

**(c) What calibration/personalization mechanisms exist?**

Existing products calibrate shallowly: connect apps, edit instructions, upload brand docs, refine via chat (Lindy/Zapier/Relevance/Beam). The strongest documented mechanisms are Anthropic's own: layered memory files (user/project/local + auto-memory), interactive `/init`, the **AskUserQuestion interview pattern**, and the **Claude-A/Claude-B skill-refinement loop** where observed failures get folded back into the skill. The winning design that no one has shipped: generic role pack + structured onboarding interview whose answers compile into a per-user calibration file (CLAUDE.local.md-style) that all the pack's skills reference, plus an observe-and-refine loop that proposes skill edits after real usage — every ingredient is documented and proven separately; the combination is open territory.
